rules.title: California Government Code Section 12955 - Housing Discrimination Prohibited
rules.requirement: It is unlawful for housing owners to discriminate or harass persons based on protected characteristics including source of income, and to use financial or income standards that fail to account for aggregate income of persons residing together equally. When government rent subsidies are involved, housing providers must base eligibility on the tenant's portion of rent and must offer applicants the option to provide alternative evidence of ability to pay instead of credit history, and consider such evidence reasonably.
rules.summary_plain: In California, landlords cannot discriminate based on your income source or credit history unfairly. If you have a government rent subsidy, they must consider your ability to pay using alternative proof, not just credit scores.
rules.summary_plain_es: En California, los propietarios no pueden discriminar injustamente basado en la fuente de sus ingresos o historial crediticio. Si tiene un subsidio de alquiler del gobierno, deben considerar su capacidad de pago usando pruebas alternativas, no solo puntajes de crédito.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to all housing accommodations in California.
rules.quoted_span: (o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following: (A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant. (B) (i) Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements. (ii) If the applicant elects to provide lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay pursuant to clause (i), the housing provider shall do both of the following: (I) Provide the applicant reasonable time to respond with that alternative evidence. (II) Reasonably consider that alternative evidence in lieu of the person’s credit history in determining whether to offer the rental accommodation to the applicant.
